notes:
Ask Claude to audit your site, and it can — Docket now speaks the Model Context Protocol.

Docket is a desktop app, and the audit has always lived behind its window. This release adds a second door: `docket mcp` serves the same engine over the Model Context Protocol, the standard AI assistants use to reach tools on your machine. Point Claude Desktop — or any MCP client — at the copy of Docket you already own, and you can ask it to audit a site in conversation and get the findings back as structured data it can reason about.

Two tools are exposed. `audit_site` crawls a site and returns the score and every finding with its severity, the pages affected, how long the fix takes and the change to make. `list_checks` answers "what does Docket actually check?" without crawling anything — all 97 of them, by area.

It is the same engine, reached a different way. There is no cloud service, no API key and no per-call charge: the crawl runs on your Mac, exactly as it does when you click the button, and the assistant is talking to the app you bought rather than to us. The page budget you ask for is the page budget you get, and `offline` keeps a run entirely local if you would rather nothing left the machine.

**Also fixed: a phone number written for machines was invisible to Docket.** A site can state its phone number twice — once in the visible page for people, and once inside its structured data for search engines, which is the copy Google actually reads for a knowledge panel. Docket's local-SEO check only ever read the visible one, so a site that put its number solely in `LocalBusiness` schema — a normal, correct thing to do — was told it had no phone number on the page at all. The check now reads both, the way its sibling address check already did.
